newsitem.title: CHINA: China vows to respect HK rights, freedoms.
newsitem.headline: China vows to respect HK rights, freedoms.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin moved to reassure the people of Hong Kong on Sunday with a pledge that Beijing would respect their rights and freedoms after China resumes sovereignty at midnight on Monday.

"We will firmly uphold the principles of 'one country, two systems' and 'Hong Kong people governing Hong Kong' as well as a high degree of autonomy," Jiang said in remarks broadcast by state television.

"We will... safeguard the Hong Kong residents' rights and freedoms in accordance with the law," Jiang said during a ceremony in Beijing's Great Hall of the People before setting off on the first leg of his journey to recover Hong Kong for China.

Jiang later flew to the border boomtown of Shenzhen, a creation of the ambitious reforms of late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping where Jiang will spend the night before entering Hong Kong late on Monday, Chinese sources in Shenzhen said.
The Hong Kong government said Jiang and Premier Li Peng would arrive in the territory on Monday afternoon.
Jiang, who is also head of the Communist Party and commander-in-chief of the armed forces, will lead China's delegation to the handover ceremonies in Hong Kong.

His departure speech underlined Beijing's repeated pledges that it would uphold the "one country, two systems" formula created by Deng Xiaoping under which Hong Kong is to retain its capitalist system unchanged for 50 years.

China has been at pains to voice its determination to maintain Hong Kong's stability in the run-up to the handover, both to demonstrate that Beijing keeps its word and to win the trust of the people of rival Taiwan for reunification.

China's resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong has sparked excitement in Beijing, where tens of thousands poured on to Tiananmen Square in the heart of the capital late on Sunday to watch a clock counting down the seconds to the handover.
Zhu Po, a worker, bowed in silent prayer to the portrait of Chairman Mao Zedong hanging above Tiananmen Gate, but said Mao should not have the credit for the return of Hong Kong.
"I think we would firstly thank Deng Xiaoping for that," she said.
Jiang, too, paid tribute to his late mentor Deng, describing the handover as a moment of glory and pride for China's people.
"Our delegation's trip to Hong Kong will surely reflect the feeling of glory and pride of all our nationalities... and reflects that our diplomatic manner is neither haughty nor humble," he said.
"(Our delegation) will successfully fulfil our lofty mission to Hong Kong without fail," Jiang said.
Jiang, who is accompanied in the delegation by Zhuo Lin, Deng's widow, pledged China would ensure the continued prosperity of the booming enclave.
"This major move... demonstrates our resolute confidence to maintain the long-term prosperity and stability of Hong Kong," he said of the decision to send such a high-level delegation.
Beijing would take charge of Hong Kong's defence and foreign affairs but would "never interfere" in its domestic affairs. Foreign business and investment would be protected, he said.
"We will explain these principal policies to our people and the rest of the world," Jiang said.

After crossing the border and within hours of the entry of 509 People's Liberation Army troops, Jiang and Premier Li are expected to sail across Victoria Harbour to Hong Kong island to receive the territory back from Britain's Prince Charles.

Jiang would attend the swearing-in of Hong Kong's new Beijing-blessed legislature just after the handover ceremony in the early hours of Tuesday before returning to Beijing for huge celebrations planned in the Chinese capital.
